name: Medal Bronze
lede: Medal Bronze is a dull yellowish brown named for the metal of coins and medals, first recorded in our library's sources in 1905.

sections.title: The metal's own brown
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates this brown to 1905, plate 14 J 7, and Ridgway's 1912 color book places the same value on plate IV, hue 19, tone m [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 files it as block 77, moderate yellowish brown [1]. Bronze itself is a copper-tin alloy; why the dictionaries paired it with "medal" is undocumented here [1].

Its closest library neighbors are [[acanthe|Acanthe]] at 4.0 units and [[khaki-grey|Khaki Grey]] at 4.1; plain [[brown|Brown]] sits 9.5 units off, a wide gap for one brown word to cover [1]. Compare [[khaki|Khaki]], [[olive|Olive]] and [[sepia|Sepia]], the names our archive finds keeping it company most often [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a color within six units of this one in 4,167, about 17.5 percent, as photographed, more common than 96 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It covers at least a third of the canvas in dozens of paintings, including Cui Zizhong's 1644 Xu Jingyang Moving His Family at 88 percent [2]. Jean-Charles Cazin has it in 12 of his 16 works here, well above the archive's overall rate [2]. The count is a color match across six centuries of photographed, varnished paintings, not a claim that any one pigment was used [2].
